title: NBC University Theater
paragraphs: A literary anthology presenting radio adaptations of important novels and plays, designed to bring major works of literature to a broad audience and at times used alongside university study programs.
Prestige literary anthology adapting major novels, short stories and plays, often with scholarly commentary and university-study/college-credit tie-ins.
GRH documents the program through NBC University Theater (July 30, 1948 to February 14, 1951) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Andrew C. Love (director on 62 recordings and performer on 1 recording), Don Stanley (announcer on 60 recordings and performer on 1 recording), Albert Harris (composer on 29 recordings and conductor on 29 recordings), Donald Morrison (performer on 28 recordings), Ben Wright (performer on 24 recordings), Ramsay Hill (performer on 22 recordings and narrator on 2 recordings), and Ernest Kinoy (writer on 12 recordings and radio adaptor on 8 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.a1cc4e5534fec5a3|WMAQ]] (aircheck from station), and [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include literature and education, class and social hierarchy, war and military conflict, family and marriage, crime and violence, and colonialism and empire.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including College-credit radio literature experiment, 1948 Peabody recognition, and Worlds Great Novels to NBC University Theater.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (135 shared credited people), [[show|escape|Escape]] (91 shared credited people), [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]] (78 shared credited people), [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (69 shared credited people), and [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]] (66 shared credited people).
